ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: <image>In $\odot A, m \angle E A D=42$. Find $m \widehat{E D B}$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle with A as the center (⊙A). Point B is at the upper left of the circle, point D is at the lower right of the circle, and segment BD passes through the center A, therefore BD is a diameter. Point E is on the right side of the circle, and radius AE and radius AD form the central angle ∠EAD labeled 42°. The problem asks for arc EDB, that is, the arc from E to B and passing through D. Reasoning: Because A is the center of the circle, ∠EAD is a central angle, and the measure of its intercepted minor arc ED is equal to 42°. Also because BD is a diameter, arc DB is a semicircle, with measure 180°. Arc EDB is composed of arc ED and arc DB, therefore m arc EDB = 42° + 180° = 222°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at A, with B-A-D collinear so BD is a diameter, and E and D adjacent on the right side of the circle. From the text, use m∠EAD = 42°. Since A is the center, ∠EAD is a central angle, so minor arc ED measures 42°. Since BD is a diameter, arc DB is a semicircle measuring 180°. The requested arc EDB is the arc from E to B passing through D, so add arc ED + arc DB = 42 + 180 = 222.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing two straight lines through center A: C-A-E and B-A-D, so BD is a diameter and AB is opposite ray AD. From the text, m∠EAD = 42°. Because AB and AD are opposite rays, ∠EAB and ∠EAD form a linear pair, so m∠EAB = 180 − 42 = 138°. Since A is the center, minor arc EB measures 138°. The requested arc EDB is the other arc from E to B, the major arc passing through D, so its measure is 360 − 138 = 222.
